subject.title: Concurrent message handling per session (async agent turns)

question: Which same-session responsiveness model should OpenClaw support when normal inbound messages arrive during an active long-running turn?
rationale: The source-level bottleneck is real, but changing it crosses transcript ordering, tool side effects, session write ownership, public config shape, and rate-limit policy, so automation cannot safely infer the product contract.

options.title: Prefer one-writer steer/yield model
options.body: Preserve one active writer per session and improve admission so urgent or short messages steer, interrupt, yield, or use explicit `/btw` at safe runtime boundaries.

options.title: Accept opt-in fast-lane concurrency
options.body: Add bounded same-session parallel turns only behind explicit config with safety tests, docs, and real Discord/channel proof.

options.title: Consolidate under broader lane issue
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53023 the canonical design thread and close narrower duplicates only after the linked PR direction is resolved.

recommendation.title: Prefer one-writer steer/yield model
recommendation.body: Preserve one active writer per session and improve admission so urgent or short messages steer, interrupt, yield, or use explicit `/btw` at safe runtime boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits in the command queue, reply runner, and config surface where history shows the strongest ownership signal.
